title: Deployment handoff timeline and post-deploy forensics template
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, operator-friendly handoff and post-deploy forensics template to use during low-latency model and infra rollouts. It combines a short timeline for the deployment window, a prioritized pre-flight checklist, a rapid smoke-and-health runbook, decision thresholds for partial rollback, and a structured post-deploy forensic checklist for the first 48h. Use this for small-to-medium rollouts (single region or limited-capacity model change). For global or multi-cluster changes, use the full runbook (link in linked_artifacts).

Quick summary of the change:
- What: Update runtime kernel selection & add quantized v2 model variant for gpt4-like aft-weights.
- Why: 18% token-cost reduction, ~5-8% median latency improvement at long sequences.
- Scope: Hosted API route /v1/generate + Dedicated pool 'dedicated-g4x-east-2' (test subset).
- Owner: Maya Ortiz (release lead)
- Backfill on-call: Priya Singh (SRE)

1) Compact deployment timeline (UTC)
- -48h: Final smoke test harness run completed and green (owner: QA).
- -24h: Release artifact build and signed, perf bench doc attached (owner: build-engineering).
- -4h: Prepare canary routing rule and config: 0.5% traffic slice with override keys staged (owner: release-eng).
- -1h: Discord/Slack announcement + tag senior on-call, coordinate channel (#release-ops-live).
- T0: Promote canary into production slice (0.5%).
- T0+10m: Evaluate initial traces and success metrics; if green -> expand to 2%.
- T0+30m: Evaluate request success, lat tail, cost-per-token; if green -> expand to 10%.
- T0+2h: If metrics stable, expand to 50% with controlled burst; keep 10% for fallback pool.
- T0+4h: Full rollout to target capacity or keep at 80% for overnight soak if high risk.

2) Pre-flight checklist (priority-ordered)
- Release artifact verified: checksum and signature verified against release manifest.
- Deployment knobs locked: autoscaler min/max, burst capacity flags, and priority-queue weights set.
- Kernel compatibility sanity: run small sequence synthetic through new kernel variant and compare outputs for token-level determinism (script: tools/kernel-smoke.sh).
- KV cache warmup plan: pre-warm top-10% prompt prefixes used by production traffic for 30m prior to T0 on canary pool.
- Traffic-slicing keys: ensure cookie/header mapping for split is stable; toggle keys documented in release comment.
- Observability tags: add release_id and variant tags to traces/metrics. Verify dashboards show new tag within 2m of emission.
- Cost-impact check: generate sample tokenization from top 50 prompts and estimate per-token cost delta; confirm within budget target.
- Health-check endpoints: /health/deps, /health/latency, token_count metrics enabled, trace sampling to 5%.
- Fallback images present: previous stable runtime and quantized model artifact available in both staging and prod registries.
- Access and escalation: confirm SRE paging roster and escalation steps in org chart.

3) Rapid smoke-and-health runbook (first 60 minutes)
- T0 -> T0+5m: smoke script (scripts/quick-smoke.sh) runs against canary slice: sanity outputs, simple generation, embeddings sanity.
- T0 -> T0+10m: pipeline scans: 95p latency, median latency, error rate (5xx+4xx), token drop count. Thresholds: errors <0.3%, median latency delta < +15ms vs baseline, 95p < +50ms.
- T0+10m -> T0+30m: sample traces for function calls that take > 120ms; check for large kv-cache misses on long sequences.
- Escalation: if error rate >0.5% or 95p latency > +80ms, pause expansion and execute rollback matrix.

4) Rollback matrix (decision table)
- Severity A: complete outage of route (5xx >1% globally) -> full rollback to last-stable within 10m; page SRE; open incident.
- Severity B: sustained tail latency degradation (95p > +200ms for 15m) -> revert variant routing to previous kernel, keep artifacts in staging; notify product.
- Severity C: correctness regressions (KL divergence on top-5 tokens > 0.08 on sample prompt set) -> halt rollout, revert model variant, begin evaluation job to diagnose.

5) Communications plan (who says what where)
- Pre-T0 (announcement): #release-ops-live post with artifact link, T0, owners, and expected impact (Maya).
- T0 live updates: minute-by-minute paging to channel by release lead: T0, T0+10m, T0+30m, T0+2h, T0+4h.
- Incident: use incident channel and runbooks in Confluence; product comms draft prepared by PM (Priya) for customer-facing comms.

6) Observability and sanity checks (dashboard quick list)
- Per-route token throughput (rps, tokens/s)
- Tail latencies: 90/95/99 percentiles by region and pool
- Error breakdown: 4xx vs 5xx and grpc/proxy failures
- Token-level cost estimate pipeline (calc routed tokens * cost-per-token)
- KV cache hit ratio and cold-start counts by model shard
- Trace sampling for top 2 slow spans: model forward, kernel memcpy, concurrency queue wait

7) Post-deploy forensic checklist (first 48h)
- 0-1h: Collect initial trace bundle from canary slices and store in release artifacts bucket with release_id tag.
- 1-6h: Run differential correctness eval on reserved prompt-set (evals/for-release-3241) and save report.
- 6-24h: Run cost aggregation and verify actual token spend vs forecast; note discrepancies >10%.
- 12-48h: Check customer-error escalations and CS tickets for pattern matching; add any sample transcripts to the forensic bundle.
- 24-48h: Consolidate logs, annotate anomalies, and produce short 'forensics summary' doc for the incident/rollout channel.

8) Minimal release notes (user-facing draft)
- Title: Faster inference for long prompts (quantized acceleration, July 2026)
- Short blurb: We rolled out a new performance-optimized variant for longer-context text generation which reduces average inference cost and improves median latency for long sequences. No breaking API changes.
- What changed: Kernel heuristics updated; a quantized model variant (v2-q8) available; default routing unchanged for existing customers.
- Impact: Most requests should see a lower per-token cost and modest latency improvements for sequences >1024 tokens. If you see regressions, please contact support with request_id and timestamp.
- Known limitations: Rare long-tail correctness differences in <0.5% of requests for highly adversarial prompts; we are monitoring and have a rollback strategy in place.

9) Post-release notes and tidy-up (owners)
- CI artifacts: mark promoted artifacts as 'released' in registry (owner: build).
- Docs: update model-catalog entry with new perf numbers and quantization notes (owner: product-docs).
- Retro: schedule 1-week retro with release team and SRE; include cost analysis and correctness eval (owner: Maya).

Appendix: quick commands and artifact locations
- smoke runner: repo/tools/quick-smoke.sh
- perf bench: s3://redwood-perf/benchmarks/bench-3241.json
- traces: ephemeral bucket with prefix release/3241/traces
- previous stable image: registry.redwood/release/stable:2026-06-28

Notes / To do (short):
- Diego: add a short health dashboard panel that includes 'kv-cache misses by shard' (due: +2d).
- Priya: confirm paging escalation contact list and update phone numbers in on-call doc (due: +1d).
- Liam: run one more deterministic kernel-compare job on long sequences (due: -4h).

End of template.
